nary_nodes.label: Ryan Gosling joins MCU as Ghost Rider
evidence: Ryan Gosling is slated to enter the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) in 2028 as he transforms into the leather-clad, motorcycle-mounted, demonic superhero Ghost Rider, Marvel announced at the San Diego Comic-Con Sunday.
nary_nodes.type_definition: An event announcing the casting of a person in a role for a film, TV show, or theatrical production.
nary_nodes.type_justification: No schema.org event type captures casting announcements; this is a specific media/entertainment industry event.

nary_nodes.label: 2026 San Diego Comic-Con announcement
evidence: Marvel Studios President Kevin Feige teased the announcement while on stage at the 2026 edition of the comic book convention...
Suddenly, the hall was plunged into darkness. To a pounding bass soundtrack, the words 'Ghost Rider' were projected onto the screen behind Feige, glowing blood red.
nary_nodes.type_justification: Comic-Con is a convention involving presentations and networking, matching schema.org's ConferenceEvent definition.

nary_nodes.label: Feige's comment on secrets and surprises
evidence: Kevin Feige teased the announcement while on stage at the 2026 edition of the comic book convention, telling fans, 'We keep secrets to maintain surprises,' before alluding to fans’ demands for the introduction of the supernatural stunt motorcyclist to the MCU.

nary_nodes.label: Ghost Rider comic book debut as Carter Slade
evidence: Ghost Rider made his Marvel comic book debut in 1967 as the 'world’s most mysterious Western hero' — the horse-riding alter ego of character Carter Slade.
nary_nodes.type_justification: A comic debut is a publication of a CreativeWork, aligning with schema.org's PublicationEvent definition.

nary_nodes.label: Ghost Rider comic book debut as Johnny Blaze
evidence: But it was as the superhero identity of the character Johnny Blaze, in Marvel Spotlight issue 5 in 1972, that Ghost Rider really set fans’ hearts aflame.
nary_nodes.type_justification: A comic debut is a publication of a CreativeWork, aligning with schema.org's PublicationEvent definition.

nary_nodes.label: 2007 Ghost Rider movie adaptation
evidence: The comic book has been adapted for the silver screen in the past, with Nicolas Cage filling the biker boots of the titular character in 2007, alongside Gosling’s now-partner, Eva Mendes, and once again in 2011.
nary_nodes.type_justification: Movie adaptations involve public screenings, which are explicitly covered by schema.org's ScreeningEvent definition.
